title: Associated graded comparison for the local Taylor map
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $M$ be a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $a\in M$ lie in an open $U\subseteq M$ with an etale coordinate chart $(t_1,\ldots,t_n):U\to\mathbf A^n_k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $R=\mathcal O_{M,a}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal, $L=R/\mathfrak m=\kappa(a)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $c=\dim_L\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Let $a_L$ be the $L$-rational point of $M_L=M\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ induced by $a$. The chart Taylor homomorphism $\tau:R\to S=L[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] is the composite of the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{M,a}\to\mathcal O_{M_L,a_L}$ with the completion of $\mathcal O_{M_L,a_L}$ at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], identified with $S$ by $T_i=t_i-t_i(a)$ [lem-trf-etale-chart-rational-point-taylor-iso]; thus $\tau(t_i)=t_i(a)+T_i$ and $\tau$ induces the identity $L\to L$ on residue fields. Choose $z_1,\ldots,z_c\in\mathfrak m$ whose classes form an $L$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Polynomial rings use [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The degree-one homogeneous parts $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_c\in L[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ of $\tau(z_1),\ldots,\tau(z_c)$ are linearly independent. The map sending $Z_j$ to the class of $z_j$ identifies $L[Z_1,\ldots,Z_c]$ with $\bigoplus_{q\ge0}\mathfrak m^q/\mathfrak m^{q+1}$. For every ideal $I\subseteq R$, set
$$J_q=((I\cap\mathfrak m^q)+\mathfrak m^{q+1})/\mathfrak m^{q+1},\qquad J=\bigoplus_{q\ge0}J_q\subseteq L[Z_1,\ldots,Z_c].$$
The ideal in $L[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ generated by the lowest nonzero total-degree homogeneous parts of elements of $IS$ is exactly $J(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_c)L[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$. For $f\in I\cap\mathfrak m^q$ its degree-$q$ Taylor part is its class in $J_q$ evaluated at the $\ell_j$. These assertions allow $a$ to be nonclosed, $c=0$ and $I=0$.

Supporting local structure: Tag 0C35 (lemma-power-series-over-residue-field), with algebra.tex Tag 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field). The displayed ideal comparison is an additional agent lemma, not asserted verbatim by either tag; it follows by splitting the formally smooth Taylor extension into c normal parameters and n-c residue-transcendence parameters.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $a$ with $C$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Write $\mathfrak p$ for $a$, and $D=\mathcal O_{M_L,a_L}=(C\otimes_kL)_{\mathfrak q}$, where $\mathfrak q$ is the kernel of $C\otimes_kL\to L$, $x\otimes\lambda\mapsto x(a)\lambda$. Then $R=C_{\mathfrak p}$ and $D$ is also a localization of $R\otimes_kL$, since every $x\notin\mathfrak p$ has nonzero image in $L$. Both rings are nonzero Noetherian local $\mathbf Q$-algebras: finite algebra generators of $C$ give finite algebra generators of $C\otimes_kL$ over $L$, so finite-type Noetherian permanence and localization apply. The stalk map $R\to D$ induces the identity on residue fields $L$. Smoothness of $M/k$ implies that $R$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); varieties.tex Tag 056S (lemma-smooth-regular); affine tensor product and localization descriptions

proof.text: The characteristic-zero field-extension theorem gives the square-zero lifting property for $k\to L$. It gives the same property for $R\to D$ explicitly: for an $R$-algebra $E$, a square-zero ideal $N\subset E$, and an $R$-algebra map $D\to E/N$, restrict to $L$ and lift that $k$-algebra map to $L\to E$. Together with the fixed map $R\to E$ this defines $R\otimes_kL\to E$. Every denominator inverted to obtain $D$ maps to a unit modulo $N$, hence to a unit in $E$: if $uv=1+e$ with $e\in N$, then $u\,v(1-e)=1$. The tensor map therefore extends to $D$ and lifts the original map. This applies in particular to maps killing a power of the maximal ideal of $D$, exactly the adic formal-smoothness condition.

source.place: Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions), characteristic-zero clause (3); agent-written tensor/localization lifting calculation

proof.text: Apply the formally-smooth local-map theorem to $R\to D$. It is flat and its closed fibre $F=D/\mathfrak mD$ is geometrically regular, hence regular (take the identity field extension). It is a nonzero Noetherian local ring; its cotangent dimension is finite, so its dimension $s$ is finite. The relative Cohen presentation applies. Put $A=\widehat R$. Since $a\in U$, $a_L$ lies in the open $U_L\subseteq M_L$, has residue field $L$, and $D=\mathcal O_{U_L,a_L}$; the etale-chart completion theorem for $t:U\to\mathbf A^n_k$, $L$ and $b=a_L$ (with $c_i=t_i(a)$) identifies $\widehat D$ with the Taylor ring $S$, $T_i\mapsto t_i-t_i(a)$, as complete local $L$-algebras for the constant coefficients; this is the identification used in the statement. The presentation supplies compatible residue sections $\alpha:L\to A$, $\beta:L\to S$, and, for $P=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_e]]$, an ideal $H\subset (X)$ and compatible isomorphisms $A\simeq P/H$ and $S\simeq L[[X,W_1,\ldots,W_s]]/H L[[X,W]]$. In these coordinates $\widehat R\to S$ is inclusion of the $X$ variables and coefficients. In particular the coefficient section $\beta$ is $\widehat\tau\alpha$; it need not be the constant coefficient embedding of the given Taylor coordinates.

proof.text: Completion makes $A$ Noetherian, complete, regular and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mA$ and residue field $L$. The completion-mod-power isomorphisms for powers 1 and 2 identify its cotangent space with $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Consequently its cotangent dimension is $c$, and the regular-local cotangent-dimension theorem gives $\dim A=c$. Nakayama applied to the finite $A$-module $\mathfrak mA$ shows that the images of $z_1,\ldots,z_c$ generate $\mathfrak mA$. Apply the specified-coefficient coordinate theorem with coefficient section $\alpha$: $L[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_c]]\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, $Z_j\mapsto z_j$. Composing with step 4 gives a complete local ring isomorphism $\Psi:L[[Z,W]]\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ taking $Z_j$ to $\tau(z_j)$, compatible with $A\to S$, and inducing the identity of residue fields.

For finitely many variables $V$, $(V)^q$ in $L[[V]]$ consists precisely of series with no monomial of total degree below $q$: one inclusion follows by multiplication, and for the other assign each monomial of degree at least $q$ to one of its finitely many degree-$q$ divisors and collect the remaining series. Hence $(V)^q/(V)^{q+1}$ is the space of degree-$q$ homogeneous polynomials, compatibly with multiplication. Since $\Psi$ and its inverse preserve maximal ideals and their powers, its associated graded map is an isomorphism $L[Z,W]\xrightarrow{\sim}L[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$. It is $L$-linear because $\Psi(\lambda)$ has residue $\lambda$. It sends $Z_j$ to $\ell_j$ and $W_i$ to the degree-one part $w_i$ of $\Psi(W_i)$. Its degree-one map is an isomorphism, so $(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_c,w_1,\ldots,w_s)$ is a basis; in particular the $\ell_j$ are independent. The same monomial calculation and completion modulo each power identify $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$ with $L[Z]$ via the prescribed classes of $z_j$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); explicit monomial description of powers of the variable ideal and induced finite-jet maps

proof.text: Let $f\in I\cap\mathfrak m^q$. Its image in $A/(\mathfrak mA)^{q+1}$ has a homogeneous degree-$q$ part $p_q(Z)$, which is exactly its class in $J_q$ under step 6. In the degree-$q$ part of $\Psi(f)$, every $Z_j$ contributes its linear part $\ell_j$, while the image of each coefficient contributes its residue; terms of degree above $q$ contribute zero. Thus the degree-$q$ Taylor part is $p_q(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_c)$, including when it is zero. The direct sum $J$ is an ideal: multiplication of a representative in $I\cap\mathfrak m^q$ by one in $\mathfrak m^r$ lies in $I\cap\mathfrak m^{q+r}$, and addition respects the displayed quotients.

source.place: Explicit homogeneous-component multiplication, as in Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian); agent-written Taylor-component calculation

proof.text: Put $K=IA\subset A=L[[Z]]$. Its initial homogeneous ideal is $J$. Indeed choose finite generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $I$ (Noetherianity was proved in step 1). For $h=\sum_i a_i f_i\in K\cap(\mathfrak mA)^q$, completion modulo power $q+1$ provides $r_i\in R$ with $a_i-r_i\in(\mathfrak mA)^{q+1}$. Then $g=\sum_i r_i f_i\in I$ and $h-g\in(\mathfrak mA)^{q+1}$. The same completion-mod-power result implies $g\in\mathfrak m^q$, so $h$ and $g$ have the same degree-$q$ class. Conversely every element of $I\cap\mathfrak m^q$ maps into $K\cap(\mathfrak mA)^q$. Thus in every degree the initial classes agree with $J_q$, not just their generated ideals.

source.place: Explicit coefficient calculation in the split power-series presentation of Tag 0C0S; agent-written initial-ideal comparison

proof.text: The map $\Psi$ takes $K A[[W]]$ onto $IS$, since it extends $R\xrightarrow{\tau}S$ and extension of an ideal twice is extension once. It preserves order and sends an initial homogeneous part through the graded isomorphism of step 6. Under that isomorphism the ideal generated by $J$ maps to the ideal generated by $p(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_c)$ for $p\in J$, namely $J(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_c)L[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$. Step 9 is therefore exactly the asserted equality of ideals of Taylor initial parts. For $I=0$ there are no nonzero initial parts and both ideals are zero. For $I=R$, $1$ supplies the unit ideal. For $c=0$, Nakayama gives $\mathfrak m=0$, so $R=L$ and its only ideals are these two cases; the polynomial identification is $L=\operatorname{gr}_0R$. Empty lists of $W$ or $T$ in the preceding coefficient calculations cause no change.
